sections.h2: Where do I go for property tax in Rowan County, KY?
sections.html:
The PVA and the sheriff both work out of the Rowan County Courthouse, 600 West Main Street in Morehead, and both keep weekday hours from 8 AM to 4 PM. The Property Valuation Administrator's office, at (606) 784-5512, assesses all taxable real and personal property, tracks ownership changes, keeps the maps and handles exemptions. The sheriff, at (606) 784-5446, mails and collects the bills.

The county government's property tax page says the sheriff's department takes cash, checks and money orders, and also credit cards through a third party. The vendor adds 2.49 percent on payments above $60, or a flat $1.50 on smaller ones. An online payment option is available if you have the bill in hand.

When a bill turns delinquent, the County Clerk and the County Attorney take over. Both offices, along with the sheriff, are described on the county's delinquent taxes page.

sections.h2: What is the Rowan County payment calendar?
sections.html:
Rowan County's published schedule differs from the plain statewide dates, because the discount window ends on November 30. The county says bills are first distributed at the beginning of November.

Rowan County sheriff's stages for a property tax bill, as listed by the county
StageWhat applies
Before November 302 percent discount
By December 31Face amount of the bill
January 1 to January 315 percent penalty
February 1 to April 1521 percent total penalty
After April 15Delinquent, sent to the County Clerk

KRS 134.015 allows the Department of Revenue to set a shifted schedule when mailing is late, which is why dates in a given year can differ from the standard November 1 cutoff. Whatever the year, the tax is the owner's personal debt from the January 1 assessment date, so a seller who closes in spring should plan to settle the year's bill.

sections.h2: How much tax does a typical Rowan County house carry?
sections.html:
The state real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. Census QuickFacts lists the median owner-occupied home in Rowan County at $161,800, so the state portion is about $171.51. The county, the school district and other taxing districts add their own rates to the final bill, and the sheriff can give the combined number for an address.

Owners 65 or older, and totally disabled owners, subtract $49,100 under the homestead exemption in 2025 and 2026. That leaves $112,700 taxable on the median home and a state share near $119.46. Apply at the PVA at the courthouse, with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport.

Only 61.5 percent of Rowan County homes are owner-occupied, so a good share of parcels are rentals. A landlord who sells should expect the buyer to ask who covers the year's bill.

sections.h2: How does Rowan County handle a delinquent tax bill?
sections.html:
After April 15 the bill belongs to the County Clerk, and the county attorney's office follows a calendar the county has published. The two notices go out on fixed days, and the sale usually falls in the second week of August.

  • May 15: the County Attorney mails a 30-day notice.
  • June 15: a 60-day notice follows if the bill is still open.
  • Second week of August: the usual sale, where third-party investors may buy a bill and add fees.
  • Each month: the delinquent amount grows by 1 percent until paid.

A taxpayer whose name is on the property can sign a delinquent tax contract with the County Attorney's office any time before three days ahead of the sale. The county requires 10 percent of the bill that same day, and the rest is divided into monthly payments. A contract signed before the clerk's sale keeps investors from purchasing the bill.

The county attorney also asserts tax claims in foreclosures, where the tax has priority status.

sections.h2: How can a Rowan County owner contest a valuation?
sections.html:
A conference with the PVA or a deputy comes first and cannot be skipped. The roll is open for public inspection for thirteen days beginning the first Monday in May, and the state requires the PVA to publish a notice in the largest local paper telling owners how to appeal. During the conference the PVA must explain how your value was derived and keep a written record.

  • File the appeal at the County Clerk's office by close of business the day after inspection ends.
  • Prepare evidence: land and building descriptions, insurance policies, construction cost, listings or sales. The board must reject an appeal that lacks it.
  • Expect a hearing 25 to 35 days after the inspection period closes, before a panel of local property owners.
  • Authorized paid agents have to fall into a statutory group such as attorneys, CPAs or licensed appraisers.

If you appeal after bills are printed, your claimed value is used for the first bill, and a supplemental bill follows if the board sets a higher number.

sections.h2: Does selling a Rowan County house wipe out back taxes?
sections.html:
No. A lien under KRS 134.420 attaches when taxes become delinquent and lasts eleven years, whoever owns the land. A title search at the County Clerk will show it, and it normally has to be cleared at closing.

The state's own example of a $1,000 bill shows how quickly a debt grows after April 15. It becomes $1,254.00 on transfer, about $1,387.79 within five business days, and $1,611.30 once the county attorney sends a first notice, before another month of interest. Compare that with paying the sheriff before the deadline.

A Rowan County owner behind on taxes has options short of the August sale: pay the sheriff, pay the clerk, or sign the contract with the County Attorney. Selling as-is for cash is a further route when repairs or inherited debts stand in the way, with the delinquent amount paid out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: What is Rowan County, Kentucky, like for sellers?
sections.html:
Rowan County was created in 1856 from parts of Fleming and Morgan counties and sits in the Eastern Kentucky Coalfield region, with about 280 square miles of land. Morehead is the seat, and Lakeview Heights is the other city. Morehead was incorporated in 1869, has close to 7,000 people, and is home to Morehead State University, Cave Run Lake, Rowan County Senior High School and St. Claire Healthcare, which the city says employs 1,200. The county touches Lewis, Carter, Elliott, Morgan, Menifee, Bath and Fleming counties, and part of the Daniel Boone National Forest lies within it.

Census QuickFacts supplies the housing picture:

  • 2025 population estimate: 24,476, down 0.7 percent from 2020.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 61.5 percent, among 9,592 households of 2.25 people.
  • Median home value: $161,800; median gross rent: $825.
  • Median household income: $54,321; 25.9 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree.
  • Building permits in 2025: 8; broadband subscriptions in 93.4 percent of households.

The 2020 census put the median age at 32.7. New construction is thin, so most listings are existing houses.

faqs.q: When is the Rowan County property tax discount deadline?
faqs.a: The county lists a 2 percent discount for bills paid before November 30. The face amount is due by December 31, and a 5 percent penalty applies through January 31.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Rowan County tax bill by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. The sheriff's department accepts Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover, with a 2.49 percent fee on payments over $60 or a flat $1.50 below that, charged by the vendor.

faqs.q: What are the Rowan County sheriff's phone and hours?
faqs.a: The sheriff's number is (606) 784-5446, at 600 West Main Street in Morehead. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 4 PM.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan for delinquent taxes in Rowan County?
faqs.a: Yes, through the County Attorney's office. You pay 10 percent of the bill on the day you sign, and the rest is spread over monthly payments. The contract must be signed before the sale.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Rowan County property assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Property Valuation Administrator at (606) 784-5512. A conference with the PVA is required before an appeal can be filed with the County Clerk.
